Graphics improvement — Micromeshes and Photon roadmap

Reference Engine Last updated: 2026-11-21 Source: graphics-roadmap.md

How to take the renderer from "good forward PBR with a screen-space GI" to dense, virtualised geometry (Micromeshes) and world-space dynamic global illumination (Photon), using only what SDL3 GPU can do on Vulkan, D3D12 and Metal.

Names: the geometry system is called Micromeshes and the GI system Photon. Both are our own designs. No code, shader text or data layout is taken from other engines; the public literature (cluster hierarchies, radiance cascades, voxel clipmaps, visibility buffers) is the only reference. This page is the graphics companion of photoreal-world-roadmap.md, which feeds it with terrain, nature and materials.

Status (2026-11-20): Micromeshes M-0, M-1 and M-2 are done (occlusion is single-phase), tested on the GPU and drawn through the real scene renderer (see micromeshes.md): RHI indirect draws and storage buffers, render stats and a HUD readout, the offline cluster hierarchy with normals, UVs, tangents and vertex colours, the GPU cut with per-instance transforms, the lit G-buffer draw and the sun cascades' own coarser cut into a shared index arena, and a single-phase occlusion test against last frame's depth. Open in M-2: two-phase occlusion and point and spot shadow cuts. Photon P-A is nearly done (P-A: the conservative voxeliser first, because the direct-light injection could not be verified before it; then motion vectors, then real direct light). Independent GPU work done meanwhile is not part of these phases: vegetation shading and wind, alpha-tested shadows, run-time material modifiers, GPU-displaced water and the weather (clouds, height fog and rain; see the Nature, Water and Environment guides). The deterministic-world foundation shared with the world roadmap (core/Hash.hpp, the scatter core) is done.

M-0 is complete. Next, in order: P-A, whose first item is the conservative voxeliser. Micromesh's next phases (M-3 streaming, the .micromesh section in .caf, a terrain cluster path to beat the benchmark's baseline) follow once the content pipeline needs them.

1. Verdict#

Photon: already under way, finish it. The engine has a compute radiance-cascade GI with a four-level voxel far field and multi-bounce feedback (PhotonCascades.hpp). The proposal to "build a GI" is mostly done; the work left is quality, validation and the world-space accuracy items its own header lists.

Micromeshes: built and drawing in the scene, with one hard limit that shaped it. The cluster hierarchy, the GPU cut with per-instance transforms, the lit G-buffer draw, shadow cascades, occlusion and the benchmark set exist (micromeshes.md). SDL3 GPU has indirect draws, storage buffers and compute passes, but no mesh shaders, no portable 64-bit atomics and no indirect-count draw, so the cut is compacted into one index arena and drawn with one hardware draw per instance (large win, low risk, as planned). A compute software rasteriser for sub-pixel triangles stays optional (M-4), using 32-bit atomics.

Dropped as written: an SDF-based GI (Photon already uses radiance cascades plus voxels; a second GI would double the maintenance), and "trillions of triangles". The realistic target is tens of millions of source triangles in view with a frame-bound cost, which is what clusters deliver.

Where it stands (2026-11-20)#

21 items done, 25 open. Micromeshes are largely done; Photon P-A is nearly done (regression scenes, voxeliser with dirty regions, real direct light, bounce gain and the Photon panel done), so the next real work on this page is Photon P-A's motion vectors (see section 8 for the order).

3. Review of the proposal#

  • "Cluster in Rust on a background thread." Wrong place. Clustering must be an engine core module (src/caffeine/micromesh) behind the C ABI, because the renderer, the .caf packer and the runtime (no Rust) all need it. The Rust editor only triggers a bake and shows stats. Generators produce plain meshes; the cluster build is the last step of the asset pipeline and is cached, never run at game time.
  • "128-256 triangles per cluster, bounds plus geometric error." Correct. Use 128 triangles and at most 128 vertices per cluster, a bounding sphere, a normal cone for back-face culling and a simplification error per cluster group, with the parent's error never smaller than its children's (monotonic), so the cut through the hierarchy is crack-free and view-independent.
  • "Compute shaders choose visible clusters and detail." Correct, and it is the core: two-phase GPU culling (previous-frame survivors first, then the rest against a fresh Min-Z pyramid) writing an indirect argument buffer. We already have the Min-Z pyramid code for GI to reuse.
  • "Software rasterisation in compute." Only for triangles that cover under about 4 pixels, and only after the hardware path works. It needs a visibility buffer with atomic min on a packed value. Without 64-bit atomics, pack 24-bit depth plus 8-bit cluster-local id into 32 bits and resolve the rest in a second pass, or skip the software path. Treat it as optional.
  • "Eliminates LOD pop-in." Only with crack-free simplification plus TAA-friendly dithered transitions. It does not remove material or shadow cost: shadow cascades must use the same cluster cut (coarser).
  • "Trillions of polygons." No. Memory (cluster data streaming) and the per-pixel cost bound it. Plan for a fixed budget (visible clusters, rasterised pixels) and measure.
  • "Foliage and alpha." Cluster rendering suits opaque geometry. Alpha-tested leaves and grass stay on the instanced path (with impostors) until a cutout-aware cluster path is justified.
  • GI "route A, SDF". Not adopted: Photon already covers it with probes plus voxels. What the SDF idea adds that we lack is accurate occlusion from off-screen and back-face geometry, which the conservative triangle voxeliser (below) provides inside the existing design.
  • GI "route B, POM GI". Only as a micro-contact term: the height maps already give POM self-shadow and a cavity term (material-pipeline.md). Extending that to a small indirect bounce in cavities is cheap and local, but it is a detail layer on top of Photon, not a GI.
  • "Anisotropic filtering, ACES, sRGB." Already in (ACES fitted, sRGB, mip chains). Only the explicit anisotropic sampler setting is worth checking.

4. Roadmap — Photon (GI)#

Photon first: it is closest to done, benefits every scene now, and Micromeshes will need its voxels.

Phase P-A — Make it correct#

Finding (2026-11-20): a prototype injected the sun into the far-field radiance (a voxel march toward the light instead of shadow maps, in photon_inject.comp) and was reverted: in a red-wall-and-floor scene the result was identical with and without it, because the screen-space cascades dominate every visible pixel and the far field only fills what leaves the screen, where the screen-depth voxel fill has no geometry. The direct light cannot be tested, and so is not worth its cost, until the conservative voxeliser (third item) provides geometry the screen does not see. Order accordingly. The Photon GI component is now reflected (Inspector, scenes, scripts: Photon GI, with Debug view), which the next attempt needs; note that Debug view did not change the image on the ComputeC0 path in that test: fixed (2026-11-21), GI only and Fallback only now work there.

  • [x] Inject real direct light (sun, point, spot) into the voxel radiance (photon_inject.comp: directLight, shadowed by a march through the material volume, the forward shader's radiance x N.L convention), with the sky ambient scaled by the sky visibility of each face. Test: a red, a white and a green wall behind the camera (not on screen) tint the white cube that faces them red, neutral and green (about 40 of 255, nothing without the wall). Three bugs found on the way, all in the far field: the probes decoded their directions twice (so the far query read other directions than the probes had traced), the cascades did the same, and the material volume was cycled (discarded) by each compute pass (CommandBuffer::beginComputePass(..., cycle)). The last one let the screened fill erase the triangle voxels every frame: a closed room read 90 of 255 of sky light, now about 15 on average (1 to 3 in the quietest frames).
  • [ ] Motion vectors pass (per object matrices, previous frame), used by Photon history, TAA and motion blur. Remove the "no motion vectors" gap; invalidate history on disocclusion by depth/normal test.
  • [x] Conservative triangle voxeliser (photon_voxelize_tri.comp, PhotonCascades::updateGeometryVoxels): one invocation per triangle, separating-axis triangle/box test over the voxels of its box, all four clipmap levels; the scene's opaque triangles are gathered with their albedo (GpuSceneRenderer::updatePhotonGeometry, one hash per object every frame, a diff against the last set) and a level is cleared and rebuilt when its clipmap origin moves or the geometry changes. Dirty regions: a moving object clears and revoxelises only the boxes where it was and is (at most 8, else the levels rebuild whole); terrain, skinned meshes (in their pose) and, on request, cut-out meshes are in the volume; past 1 million triangles the voxeliser stops and the screened fill works alone, and the panel says so. A textured surface counts with the mean colour of its picture (GpuTextureCache::averageColor). GPU tests: test_photon_voxelizer.cpp. The screened fill stays, as the fallback and for the terrain.
  • [x] Headless regression scenes: Cornell box, light-through-door, thin wall leak (module photon_gi in windows/main/tests.rs, image thresholds on the difference between GI off and on). Measured 2026-11-21: colour bleed passes (a white floor gains about +8 red beside the red wall, +6 green beside the green one). A room with no opening leaked: with the camera inside it the interior was lit like the open sky (gains of 60 to 90 out of 255, whatever the sky intensity); sealed now (about 15 on average over the frames; single frames swung between 3 and 25 until probes got their own sample offsets, see the temporal average in the Photon guide), with the sun's bounce through a slit at 7 to 16 on the far floor against about 170 on the lit patch, and a partition shuts that bounce out of the far side (4.3 -> 1.5). The far field is asked from 0.4 m off the surface (the surface's own voxels are up to 0.5 m thick) and from the ray's origin, not its screen-exit point. All regular tests.
  • [x] Bounce gain and the Photon panel (C ABI v17: caffeine_session_photon_stats, caffeine_session_photon_rebuild). Bounce gain scales what the voxels hold: on the far floor of the slit room (GI only, of 255) it reads 13 at gain 0, 18 at 1 and 24 at 4; the screen cascades are scaled by Intensity. The Photon tab edits the component, the voxel geometry switches and presets, with live voxel statistics; see photon-guide.md.

Phase P-B — Quality and stability#

  • [ ] Normal-aware spatial-temporal denoise of the SH resolve; clamp fireflies; ghosting metrics in tests.
  • [ ] Emissive surfaces as lights (materials already have emissive maps).
  • [ ] Sky as a proper source: feed the prefiltered environment (split-sum) to Photon far field and to specular IBL, one source of truth.
  • [ ] Glossy reflections from the probe field when screen-space tracing misses (replaces the per-object probe cubemaps as the fallback, so off-screen reflections stay stable).
  • [ ] Per-view scratch resources (the header notes one shared scratch instance); needed for editor previews and split view.

Phase P-C — Scale and cost#

  • [ ] Quality tiers with measured GPU budgets (Eco/Low/Balanced/High) and a frame-time governor.
  • [ ] Clipmap far field following the camera with toroidal updates; larger worlds without re-fill spikes.
  • [ ] Feed terrain and vegetation chunks (from the world roadmap) into the voxel volume as they stream in.
  • [ ] Update the website Photon page to the real state and add the new knobs to the editor UI with UiIds.

5. Roadmap — Micromeshes (virtual geometry)#

Each phase ships alone and keeps the old path as a fallback behind a flag.

Phase M-0 — RHI and tooling prerequisites#

  • [x] rhi/CommandBuffer wraps indirect draws (drawIndirect, drawIndexedIndirect, multi-draw count), indirect dispatch, graphics storage buffers for the vertex and fragment stages and compute passes with read-write storage buffers; BufferUsage::{Indirect, IndirectWrite, GraphicsStorage, GraphicsStorageWrite}; RenderDevice::capabilities() (indirect draw and dispatch, storage, no mesh shaders, no 64-bit atomics) and readBuffer. Tested on the GPU in tests/test_rhi_indirect.cpp: indirect arguments decide what is drawn, and a compute pass writes the draw arguments (a miniature of GPU culling). The tests skip without a GPU or glslc.
  • [x] CPU-side pass timers per stage (gather, shadows, opaque, translucent, total) and counters (meshes, frustum culled, draw calls, instanced draw calls, triangles) in GpuSceneRenderer::lastFrameStats(); C ABI v11 caffeine_session_render_stats, the Rust Engine::render_stats() and the agent query render_stats. SDL3 GPU has no portable GPU timestamps, so the times are encoding time, not GPU time.
  • [x] The viewport HUD shows the last frame's triangles, draws and Micromesh draws (cheap counters, no read-back). Still open: Profiler entries and a panel with the cluster counters.
  • [x] The reproducible benchmark set (./scripts/benchmark-micromesh.sh): a dense rock field, a forest of 300 dense trees and a terrain at two grid sizes, fixed camera paths, content generated in code (no assets, byte-identical every run, tested), every renderer path that applies. Triangle and draw counts reproduce exactly; wall time is a whole frame including read-back, encode time the CPU's. Results in micromeshes.md: Micromesh draws 6.1x (rocks) and 3.3x (forest) fewer triangles and a median frame of 0.56 and 0.75 of the instanced one, but the forest costs more CPU (one draw per tree); the terrain baseline is 0.2 to 0.8 M triangles in 100 to 400 draws. The old assets/benchmarks (an unused 43 KB scene) is not part of it.

Phase M-1 — Cluster build (offline, core)#

  • [x] micromesh module (src/caffeine/micromesh/Micromesh.hpp): clusters of at most 128 triangles and 128 vertices along a Morton curve (our own, simpler than a greedy adjacency split), each with a tight bounding sphere, a back-face normal cone and a local vertex remap (one byte per index).
  • [x] Hierarchy: clusters are grouped (4 at a time, widened when a group cannot shrink), each group is merged, simplified by quadric edge collapse with its boundary locked (and non-manifold edges), and split again, up to one root. A group's error is the larger of its collapse error and its children's, plus an epsilon, so it is strictly monotonic; its sphere contains the children's. A cut is "own error <= threshold < parent error" (optionally divided by the distance to the sphere for a projected error).
  • [x] Versioned POD bytes: serialize / deserialize (bounds-checked), byte-identical rebuilds. C ABI v12 caffeine_micromesh_build (positions, indices, stats, bytes) and the Rust Engine::micromesh_build, so generators and a packer can bake. Not done: the .micromesh section inside .caf and a caf-pack CLI (a separate submodule repo).
  • [x] Tests (tests/test_micromesh.cpp, 9 cases): limits per cluster, every level coarser, one root on closed meshes, monotonic errors and sphere containment, every cut of a sphere and a torus is closed and manifold (each edge in exactly two triangles) at 12 thresholds, view-dependent cuts are crack-free and coarser far away, an open grid keeps its boundary and terminates, back-face cones never hide a facing cluster, degenerate input, byte-identical rebuilds and the ABI.
  • [ ] Known limits: groups are neighbours on a Morton curve, not an adjacency graph, so a level removes about half the triangles on compact meshes and less on thin or branching ones; open meshes stop where their locked boundary pins everything (several roots); a collapse picks the best of the two endpoints and the midpoint (no optimal position); measured on meshes up to 82 k triangles (about a second to build 80 000); locked UV seams limit how far a mesh with many islands reduces. (Normals, UVs, tangents and vertex colours are carried now.)

Phase M-2 — GPU culling and hardware draw#

  • [x] Upload to GPU buffers (render/MicromeshGpu): one storage buffer of cluster records (bounds, error spheres, cone, index range), one position buffer, one index buffer with every cluster's global indices, and an indirect-argument buffer.
  • [x] Per-instance transforms: MicromeshGpu::setInstances, cull index instance * clusterCount + cluster, per-instance cut, frustum and cone, one dispatch and one indirect draw for the whole field (196 rocks, 16 M source triangles: 0.15 to 0.5 M drawn per frame, 10x fewer than the exact mesh on average). Images and GIF in micromeshes.md. Still one hierarchy per object and a uniform scale per instance.
  • [x] Compute pass 1 (shaders/micromesh_cull.comp): per cluster, the cut test (own error within the threshold, parent's not, optionally projected by distance), frustum test and back-face cone; it writes one indexed-draw argument set per cluster with indexCount 0 when culled, so the CPU issues the same drawIndexedIndirect(args, 0, clusterCount) every frame with no read-back and no atomics.
  • [x] Occlusion, single-phase: each frame the previous depth buffer becomes a farthest-depth pyramid (MicromeshHzb, one storage buffer) and the camera's compacting cull drops clusters whose sphere is behind it (Mesh Renderer -> Micromesh occlusion, off by default). Behind a wall: 1.5x to 2.5x fewer triangles (2.1x mean), picture difference 0.11 / 255 mean; a cluster that becomes visible shows one frame late at silhouette edges. Images in micromeshes.md.
  • [ ] Two-phase occlusion (draw last frame's visible clusters, rebuild the pyramid from that depth, test the rest): removes the one-frame lag; needs the opaque pass split in two.
  • [x] The indirect draw works on the GPU: MicromeshGpu::draw binds the buffers and issues one multi-draw over every cluster. Tested on the GPU (tests/test_micromesh_gpu.cpp): the cut the compute pass selects equals the CPU's selectCut at 4 distances x 3 thresholds, the cone filter equals isBackFacing, the frustum test equals the same sphere-plane test on the CPU, a farther camera picks a coarser cut, and a rendered cut covers the sphere's disc (fine and coarse alike).
  • [x] Prerequisite for it: shading normals carried through every collapse and drawn with MicromeshGpu::drawLit; a coarse cut shades within 1.6 to 10 / 255 of the exact mesh (facets: 2.9 to 13). UVs are carried too (seams stay locked): a bump map and a UV checker stay within 1.2 to 11.7 / 255 of the exact render across the cuts. Images in micromeshes.md. Tangents, vertex colours and a second UV set are still missing.
  • [x] Draw the visible clusters into the existing G-buffer targets through the scene pipeline (Photon, SSAO, TAA and post keep working unchanged): Mesh Renderer -> Micromesh (+ error in px) draws the mesh as a cut through scene_lit.frag, one indexed draw per instance (the cull pass compacts the cut: SDL3 GPU has no indirect-count draw). 81 lit, shadowed rocks: 5.3x to 7.1x fewer triangles per frame for the camera, 10.8x from the air, picture difference 1.5 / 255. Details, the benchmark table and the limits in micromeshes.md. Also fixed on the way: a dense mesh without materials re-read its file on every draw of every frame (4 to 8 ms of CPU per draw).
  • [x] Shadow cascades draw their own coarser cut (same hierarchy, so no cracks): the sun's cascades are cut at four shadow texels by shadow_micromesh.vert, into a shared index arena that grows by itself (32 MB for 81 rocks instead of one full-size index buffer per rock). Point and spot shadows still draw the full mesh. Also: non-uniform scale, one hierarchy per sub-mesh, vertex colours carried. The editor viewport renders without shadow maps unless ViewportSettings::shadows is on (C ABI v14).
  • [ ] Point and spot shadow maps draw their own coarser cut too (only the sun's cascades do).
  • [ ] Terrain tiles and Nature rocks/trunks are first adopters; foliage stays instanced. (Rocks and trunks can opt in through the Mesh Renderer, and the Nature generator switches it on for the solid parts it places (3 000 triangles or more); terrain has no cluster path: its baseline is in the benchmark set.)

Phase M-3 — Streaming and memory#

  • [ ] Page cluster data in and out by distance and error with a fixed memory budget and an async upload queue; never stall a frame.
  • [ ] Geometry compression (quantised positions and octahedral normals) and an LRU of pages.
  • [ ] Hook the world chunks: a chunk's baked meshes are clustered when first cached and reused afterwards.

Phase M-4 — Small-triangle path (optional, measure first)#

  • [ ] Compute rasteriser for clusters whose triangles are under ~4 pixels, writing a visibility buffer with 32-bit atomics and a resolve pass that fetches attributes. Gate on a measured win over the hardware path on dense rock/bark scenes.
  • [ ] Material resolve in screen tiles to avoid one pass per material.

Phase M-5 — Editor integration#

  • [x] Inspector toggle "Micromesh" on a Mesh Renderer (reflection exposes Micromesh and Micromesh error (px)); still open: a stats panel and a debug view (cluster colours, error cut, culled clusters), UiId catalogue entries for the toggle and MCP actions.
  • [ ] Nature, Terrain and Water generators export through the cluster build. Nature is done: its Micromesh option places solid parts of 3 000 triangles or more with Micromesh on, and Merge parts gives a tree one mesh with a material slot per part. Terrain and Water are open.
  • [ ] Docs and headless captures (cluster debug view) in the site.

6. Shared items#

  • [ ] One visibility source: the cluster cull and Photon voxelisation read the same instance data.
  • [ ] Frame graph light: explicit pass list with resource lifetimes so culling, G-buffer, Photon, shadows and post are ordered and memory is reused; today the order is hand-written.
  • [ ] Quality governor: one setting maps to Photon tier, shadow resolution, cluster error threshold, and runtime scalers (resolution, TAA upsampling).
  • [ ] Reference scenes with fixed seeds rendered headless and compared as visual baselines.

7. Risks#

Risk Mitigation
No mesh shaders, no 64-bit atomics in SDL3 GPU hardware indirect draws first; software raster optional and 32-bit
Cracks between LOD groups locked group boundaries, monotonic error, tests that cut at random thresholds
Photon history ghosts with moving objects motion vectors, disocclusion tests, regression scenes
Voxeliser cost on dynamic geometry static baked once, dynamic dirty-region updates only
Two geometry paths drift apart flag-gated, same G-buffer output, shared tests
Scope Photon P-A and Micromeshes M-0/M-1 are independent and can run in parallel

8. Suggested order#

Done: M-0, M-1 and M-2 (Micromeshes, up to single-phase occlusion). From here:

  1. P-A (correct Photon): the conservative voxeliser first, then motion vectors, then real direct light and the regression scenes. Nothing of Photon is done, and every Micromesh and world item that wants GI waits on it.
  2. M-5, the cheap part: the Terrain and Water generators switching Micromesh on (Nature does), stats panel and debug view, UiIds, site captures. Also the .micromesh section in .caf (a cache for the first-frame build) and a terrain cluster path to beat the benchmark.
  3. P-B, then M-3 (streaming and compression) tied to the world chunks of the world roadmap.
  4. P-C, two-phase occlusion and point/spot shadow cuts, and M-4 only if profiling asks for it.
